slides.title: Arabica vs robusta: what you taste
slides.subtitle: Taste, body and crema. One myth falls along the way.

slides.title: Body: the weight in your mouth
slides.body: Robusta usually feels heavier and rounder. Arabica feels lighter and more delicate. That extra body is why some blends for milk drinks include a little robusta.
slides.highlight: Body is how heavy coffee feels on your tongue.

slides.title: Crema: who makes more?
slides.body: Crema is the light-brown foam on top of an espresso. Robusta usually gives more of it, which is one reason many espresso blends include some.
slides.highlight: More robusta usually means thicker crema.

slides.myth: Robusta is always the cheap, bad coffee.
slides.truth: Quality varies by farm and processing, for both species. Good robusta can add body and crema, and many espresso blends use a little on purpose.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Check your espresso bag: does it say 100% arabica, or list robusta? Then taste for sweetness, body and crema.

slides.title: Nuance or body?
slides.body: Arabica brings sweet, tangy notes. Robusta brings body and crema. Many blends use both.
